rows.description: A wise team or family welcomes a newcomer with a simple, warm ritual and explains its meaning. Explaining the unwritten habits helps them feel included and not tested.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 1–3, 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A teenager who feels odd offline discovers a community about their interest and feels understood for the first time. The belonging is real and can be a lifeline.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A teenager follows only accounts that agree with them and begins to think everyone thinks the same. Feeds reward what feels good to see, so the picture of the world narrows without their noticing.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A teenager who is mocked in a group chat or game lobby feels trapped, since leaving means losing friends. They often hide it from adults for fear of losing their device.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A young adult finds that harsher posts get more likes and shares, so their tone hardens. The audience shapes the speaker, and the speaker starts performing outrage.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.subtype: Banned or blocked from a group [Receiver]
rows.description: A person removed from an online community feels rejected, angry and sometimes relieved. Being cut off from a source of belonging stings even when the rule was fair.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: anger, relief, nostalgia

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A young adult deliberately follows a few thoughtful people who disagree and checks claims from more than one source. They tolerate the discomfort of being unsure.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 23–26

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A young adult moderating a community feels responsible and stretched, and is criticised whatever they decide. Clear written rules, consistency and patience protect both moderator and members.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.subtype: Parent or friend noticing a change [Observer]
rows.description: A parent or friend sees someone's language and mood harden after spending hours in a particular online group. Curiosity and conversation work better than confiscation, and serious concern warrants qualified help.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22

rows.subtopic: Online communities, echo chambers and moderation
rows.description: A person notices that a group leaves them anxious or angry and steps away, keeping the real friends by other means. Choosing peace over a group's approval is a mature act.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 13–17, 18–22
related mind states: anger, anxiety, calm
